faq.q: Which citation styles and source types are supported?
faq.a: Six styles: APA 7th, MLA 9th, Chicago (both Notes-Bibliography and Author-Date), Harvard, IEEE and Vancouver. Source types include book, book chapter, journal article, website, newspaper, thesis, conference paper, report, government document, YouTube video, podcast and interview. The input fields change to match the source type you pick, and it also outputs the matching in-text or footnote form.

faq.q: Will it look up a book or article from a DOI or ISBN?
faq.a: No — the DOI/ISBN box is an offline helper only. It tells you whether what you pasted looks like a DOI or an ISBN and which fields to fill in manually, but it does not fetch any data online. Everything runs in your browser, so you type the author, title, year and other details yourself.

faq.q: How does it format author names and multiple authors?
faq.a: It applies each style's rules automatically. APA converts names to Surname, Initials and uses an ampersand before the last of up to 20 authors (with an ellipsis for 21+); MLA uses 'et al.' for three or more; Chicago and Harvard join with 'and'; IEEE and Vancouver number and cap the list with 'et al.' past six. Enter authors separated by semicolons, & or 'and'.

faq.q: Can I build a full reference list?
faq.a: Yes. 'Add to Bibliography' collects citations, stored in your browser under citeBib. Numbered styles (IEEE, Vancouver) keep citation order; the others are sorted alphabetically. You can edit or delete entries, copy the whole list, download it as a .txt, or export a basic BibTeX file. The bibliography survives a page reload.
